newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-WEBB THREE CLEAR IN WOMEN'S BRITISH OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WEBB THREE CLEAR IN WOMEN'S BRITISH OPEN.

text.p: Australia's Karrie Webb continued her love affair with the British Open on Thursday when she fired a seven- under-par first round 65 to lead by three shots.

The 22-year-old, a shock winner of the tournament at Woburn two years ago, collected seven birdies in heatwave conditions to finish the day three clear of Britain's Trish Johnson and 1994 champion Liselotte Neumann of Sweden.

"It was the win that gave my career the kick-start, so I'm always going to have great memories of the Open," said the young Queenslander, who went on to become the first rookie to pass the million-dollar mark in earnings when she topped the 1996 U.S. LPGA Order of Merit.
Webb had a great day with the putter. Five of her seven birdies came from long range and included a purple patch of four in a row from the second in a brilliant outward nine of 31.
Less happy was Johnson, who followed her 68 with a vitriolic attack on some of her fellow professionals.
After a round lasting five hours 15 minutes, she claimed: "It was misery. The pace of play was hideous. Anyone who can't get round in under four hours deserves to be shot.
"It must drive spectators to absolute boredom."

American defending champion Emilee Klein was four off the pace with a 69, while Sweden's world number one Annika Sorenstam salvaged a par 72 when she came close to holing her second shot at the 18th for the easiest of tap-in birdies.
